about: Editor nodes of nonoha-editor: display and input nodes that live outside the engine graph. Single source for the editor's node registry and add menu; also served as /editor-nodes.json and shipped in editor_html for tools and AI agents.
layout: settings.nodes[<id>] = {type, x, y, width?, height?, label?, data: {<settings>}}; label is the title shown (defaults to the id). Keep editor nodes outside the $graph frame (settings.nodes.$graph = {width, height}).
grid: Positions are on a 20 px grid: x and y (a node's top-left) are multiples of 20. Every node has its ports in 20 px rows, the first one centered 50 px below the node's top (30 px on a graph port node): nodes at the same y have their rows in line, and ports of the same row join with a straight line. A waypoint ($wp:<id>) stores its center: x and y are 10 plus a multiple of 20, which is a row's center. Engine nodes, graph ports and waypoints are relative to the $graph frame (itself on the grid); editor nodes are absolute.

connections.fromOutputPort: Input handles connect from $output:<port> nodes of the graph. Stored in settings.editor_edges: key '<source>-<target>:<targetHandle>', value {source, sourceHandle: null, target, targetHandle}. Values arrive complete (same values the app sees).
connections.fromEngineNode: With engines that report inspector capabilities (1.1+), input handles can also connect straight from an engine node output (source '<Node>', sourceHandle '<port>'). Drawn dashed; values are sampled by the inspector and can miss updates.
connections.toInputPort: Output handles of input nodes connect to $input:<port> nodes.
connections.limit: Each input handle takes one connection.

nodes.label: View
nodes.description: Hosts a view: a read-only display that draws the values of its inputs. Views come from plugins (static/views/manifest.json; `nonoha ws catalog` lists them) or are built in (builtinViews below). Its input handles are the view's inputs, each taking one value of any of the types in accepts; delivery says whether the view needs every value or the latest (then it gets the current value first). data.settings holds the view's settings (keys and ranges as the view declares them).

view.description: <plugin id>/<view id> (e.g. cv_nodes/flow-overlay) or builtin/<view id>
